context: Radial edge-bundled dependency network with 6 modules, 283 leaf nodes, and 829 edges rendered via WebGL instanced quads. A tension slider controls bundling from hairball to straight lines; hovering a node highlights its connections by dimming all others.
first_impression: Clean and well-structured in its static state — the module-colored ring is immediately legible — but the WebGL edge layer appears entirely invisible in the screenshot, making the default view information-free without interaction.
what_works: The 6-color Tol palette is comfortably within perceptual limits and module groupings on the ring are immediately distinguishable by color arc. The progressive-disclosure interaction model (dim all, highlight one neighborhood) is exactly right for 829 edges — it collapses the density problem rather than fighting it.
what_doesnt: Node labels at 6.5px / 55% opacity are below readable size on any normal display, and synthetic IDs like 'sub0.06' carry no semantic value — the label layer adds visual noise without informational payoff. The static (non-hover) state is nearly useless since edges render at alpha 0.06–0.34 and appear invisible in the screenshot, meaning the visualization's entire value is gated behind interaction with no ambient signal of edge density or cross-module coupling.
